SELECT 
  fish_date_doy,
  cls,
  COUNT(*) as num_trips,
  SUM(yt) as total_yt,
  ROUND(AVG(yt), 2) as avg_yt_per_trip,
  MAX(yt) as max_yt_single_trip
FROM trips
WHERE fish_date_doy >= 92 AND fish_date_doy <= 120
  AND fish_date_season = 2
GROUP BY fish_date_doy, cls
ORDER BY fish_date_doy, cls
LIMIT 200;

SELECT 
  boat,
  cls,
  fish_date_doy,
  yt,
  anglers
FROM trips
WHERE fish_date_doy >= 105 AND fish_date_doy <= 120
  AND yt > 5
ORDER BY fish_date_doy DESC, yt DESC
LIMIT 30;

import pandas as pd

# Get the trips table
trips = tables['trips']

# Filter to season 2 and look at the spring run period (DOY 92-110)
spring_run = trips[(trips['fish_date_season'] == 2) & (trips['fish_date_doy'] >= 90) & (trips['fish_date_doy'] <= 115)]

# Aggregate by class and DOY to see patterns
by_class_doy = spring_run.groupby(['fish_date_doy', 'cls']).agg({
    'yt': 'sum',
    'anglers': 'sum',
    'boat': 'count'
}).round(2)

print("=== SPRING RUN SUMMARY (DOY 90-115) ===")
print(by_class_doy.tail(20))

# Look at what boats caught the most fish
print("\n=== TOP BOATS BY TOTAL YT (DOY 90-115) ===")
top_boats = spring_run.groupby('boat').agg({
    'yt': 'sum',
    'anglers': 'mean',
    'boat': 'count'
}).sort_values('yt', ascending=False).round(2)
top_boats.columns = ['total_yt', 'avg_anglers', 'num_trips']
print(top_boats.head(15))

# What share would 0.6117 fish be?
print("\n=== HYPOTHETICAL: How to get 0.6117 fish ===")
# If you got 1 trip on a boat with 62 anglers that caught 38 YT
# Your share = 38 / (62 + you + others)
# With you and say 11 competitors, share = 38 / (62 + 1 + 11) = 38/74 = 0.514
# But if the boat had 45 anglers and 38 YT and 11 competitors:
# share = 38 / (45 + 1 + 11) = 38/57 = 0.667
print("38 YT on a 45-angler boat with 11 competitors = 38 / (45+1+11) =", 38/57)
print("35 YT on a 50-angler boat with 4 competitors = 35 / (50+1+4) =", 35/55)
